text: Working with APIs is a common task for developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually with methods like GET or POST. The server often returns data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use in your code. Before you can access the data, you usually need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. Many APIs also have rate limits, meaning you can only send a certain number of requests per minute. Finally, good error handling is important, so your program can respond properly when something goes wrong.
